user_questions.question: Where does the order dollar amount come from? Loyalty_Transaction__c has no link to any order. Options: (a) standard Order.TotalAmount via a new lookup (Order has 0 records); (b) Transaction__c.Total_Amount__c via a new lookup (0 records, sale/refund object); (c) the Pronto app sends the order amount in its payload when it creates the loyalty transaction, stored on a new Loyalty_Transaction__c.Order_Amount__c field. Evidence: Apex class comments say Pronto orders live in the external Heroku Orders API. Recommendation: (c).
user_questions.simulated_answer: When the Pronto app posts an order, an Earn loyalty transaction is created; the order total comes from the app payload. I assumed the order data was in Salesforce, but it would come from the app payload.

skill_friction: Step 5 says 'If you can write a recommendation for the question, you have a basis: do not ask', but also lists 'two interpretations need different objects' as an example that warrants asking. Here I could write a recommendation (Pronto payload) yet the choice changed the target object (Order vs Transaction__c vs new field), so the two rules conflict; I asked.

Intent says the Pronto app 'creates' the Earn transaction; the requirement says points are awarded when the transaction is created. The skill gives no guidance on whether the external creator's payload change counts as an 'undeliverable responsibility' that should be asked about or just recorded; I recorded it as blocking for delivery.
No guidance on whether a test ApexClass should be added for a flow-only inventory (Rule 4 minimal design vs production flow-coverage requirement); AskCoworker T said no test needed and I added one.
Whether a new field written only by an integration needs layout placement is unclear; the content rule allows 'Section 8 says why not', which I used, but the default is not stated.
